case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment's caption.

number_of_accused.reason: Judgment refers throughout to a single appellant-accused.

accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to as male ('his' throughout).

accused_age.correct_value: 27 at conviction; 22 at time of offence (per appellant's counsel)
accused_age.quote: at the time of the commission of the offence, the appellant's age was 22 years
accused_age.reason: 27 is the trial court's age at conviction; the age at offence is 22, which the value omits.

accused_religion.reason: Religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.reason: Appellant is described as the driver.

previous_criminal_record.reason: Judgment notes the accused has no antecedents and this was his first offence.

victim_age.reason: Judgment states the victim's life was cut short at age 28.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: the appellant, who was the driver, that the vehicle operating on route no.131 was not available
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Judgment shows a driver-passenger encounter via employer transport; it never describes them as strangers.

offence_category.quote: The prosecution successfully established the charge of the offence of rape, punishable under Section 376 of the IPC as well as the offence under Section 366 of IPC
offence_category.reason: Value captures only rape; the case also involved kidnapping (s.366) and murder (s.302).

statutory_provisions.quote: convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 366, 376 and 302 of the Indian Penal Code
statutory_provisions.reason: Value omits section 366, under which the appellant was also convicted.

weapon.reason: No weapon is mentioned in the judgment.

evidence_type.correct_value: Recovery of body and clothing/footwear at appellant's instance; no medical evidence mentioned
evidence_type.quote: Ultimately, her dead body was recovered at the instance of the appellant. The clothes on the person of the deceased, footwear, etc. were found near the dead body.
evidence_type.reason: Recovery is supported, but medical evidence is not mentioned anywhere in the judgment.

confession.reason: Judgment never mentions a confession; 'None' asserts an absence the text does not address.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Brutal nature of the crime; facts shock the conscience; undue leniency would undermine public confidence
aggravating_circumstances.quote: showing undue leniency in such a brutal case will adversely affect the public confidence in the efficacy of the legal system
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Judgment expressly identifies brutality and public-confidence concerns as aggravating factors.

mitigating_circumstances.correct_value: Age (27 at conviction), wife and small child, aged parents, first offence, no antecedents
mitigating_circumstances.quote: he had a wife and small child as well as aged parents
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Trial court's mitigating factors (family, age, first offence) are stated in the judgment.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Judgment states rigorous imprisonment for rest of life by the Sessions Judge.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: Dismissed both the appellant's appeal and the State's enhancement appeal
high_court_outcome.quote: The High Court, by the impugned judgment, dismissed both appeals.
high_court_outcome.reason: Judgment states the High Court dismissed both appeals, not 'not applicable'.

final_outcome.correct_value: Convicted; sentence modified to life imprisonment with release only after 30 years of actual sentence
final_outcome.quote: We direct that the appellant shall undergo imprisonment for life. We also direct that the appellant shall be released only after he completes thirty years of actual sentence.
final_outcome.reason: 'Convicted' omits that the Supreme Court modified the sentence and partly allowed the appeal.

offence_finally_established.quote: The appellant–accused was also convicted for the offence under Section 302.
offence_finally_established.reason: Value lists only rape; judgment confirms conviction on ss.366, 376 and 302.

imprisonment_type.reason: Supreme Court imposed a fixed-term sentence of thirty years.

imprisonment_years.reason: Thirty years is the fixed term directed.

fine_rs.reason: No fine is mentioned in the judgment.

neutral_facts.correct_value: A driver for a Bengaluru company drove a female employee working late hours, who was reported missing and later found dead; the accused was convicted of kidnapping, rape and murder and sentenced to life imprisonment; the trial court's sentence was challenged in appeal.
neutral_facts.quote: The high court did not review the case, and the supreme court modified the sentence to a fixed term of thirty years.
neutral_facts.reason: Says High Court did not review the case, but it dismissed both appeals; also reveals the Supreme Court's outcome.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment notes the offence is punishable with death penalty or life imprisonment.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Constitutional Courts can impose a modified fixed-term sentence even where death penalty is not imposed, with a term not less than 14 years (s.433A Cr.P.C.)
legal_principle_applied.quote: even in a case where capital punishment is not imposed or is not proposed, the Constitutional Courts can always exercise the power of imposing a modified or fixed-term sentence
legal_principle_applied.reason: Value states the Sriharan limitation, but the Court's applied principle expands the power beyond death-penalty cases.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Sriharan followed; Shraddananda, Sahib Hussain and Gurvail Singh cited with matching citations.

sentencing_rationale.reason: Matches the Court's reasoning on fixed term to exclude remission, given gravity and other factors.
